name: Mastercard
look: Warm cream canvas, extreme radii as the design language, circular portraits on traced orbital paths, ghost watermark headlines.

hero.title: There are some things money can't buy. For everything else.
hero.sub: Cadence connects two hundred million merchants to three billion cardholders across two hundred and ten countries, and settles it in about four hundred milliseconds.

features.title: A network, not a bank
features.sub: We do not issue the card or hold the account. We move the authorisation, the clearing and the settlement between the people who do.

items.title: Authorisation
items.body: A request routed from terminal to issuer and back in about four hundred milliseconds, at any hour, in any of two hundred and ten markets.

items.title: Fraud scoring
items.body: A risk decision computed on network-wide signal in the same round trip, so a legitimate customer is not stopped at the till.

items.title: Cross-border
items.body: Currency conversion at the network rate with the margin published, rather than folded invisibly into the exchange rate.

items.title: Tokenisation
items.body: The card number never reaches the merchant. A token scoped to that merchant does, and it is useless anywhere else.

items.title: Developer APIs
items.body: Sandbox credentials in about two minutes, and forty-one APIs documented with real request and response payloads.

items.title: Dispute resolution
items.body: A structured chargeback process with defined evidence requirements and a published clock at every stage.

showcases.title: Accept payments in two hundred and ten markets
showcases.body: One integration reaches every market we operate in, with local acquiring where it lowers the cost and cross-border rails where it does not. The routing decision is made per transaction, and the reasoning is visible in the reporting.

showcases.title: Sandbox credentials in two minutes
showcases.body: Forty-one APIs with documented rate limits, real payloads and a sandbox that returns the same decline codes production does — including the awkward ones you only find out about at three in the morning.
points: Webhook replay for the last thirty days

gallery.title: Where it works
gallery.sub: Two hundred million merchant locations, from a market stall to a global retailer.

testimonial.quote: We asked four networks what their cross-border margin actually was. One of them answered with a number and a page explaining how it was calculated. That is the one we integrated.
testimonial.name: Yusuf Demir

pricing.title: Work with us
pricing.sub: Interchange is set by the network and published. What you pay your acquirer is between you and them.

tiers.name: Developer
tiers.desc: Sandbox access and the full API surface.

items.a: No. Cards are issued by banks and licensed institutions. We operate the network that carries the authorisation, clearing and settlement between the issuer, the acquirer and the merchant.
By the network, published per region and per card category, and updated on a fixed annual schedule. It is paid by the acquirer to the issuer — we do not receive it.
The merchant stores a token scoped to them rather than the card number. If their systems are breached, the token cannot be used anywhere else, and the underlying card does not need reissuing.
Each stage has a published clock — typically 30 days for the initial chargeback and 45 for representment. The tooling shows which stage a case is in and what evidence is still outstanding.

cta.title: Let's talk about what you're building
cta.sub: Sandbox credentials take about two minutes. A conversation takes slightly longer.

notes: Extreme radius is the design language: 20px on body CTAs, 40px on cards, 99px and 1000px on pills and portraits. Anything square reads as a third-party embed.
The brand red and yellow belong to the logo mark only. Putting either on a button or a surface breaks the identity — the UI palette is cream, ink and one orange.
Signal orange is the single aggressive colour, reserved for consent actions and the eyebrow dot. It is a cue, never a fill.
Circular portraits sit on traced orbital arcs with small white satellite CTAs attached to their edge — the signature compositional move.
Ghost watermark headlines (cream on cream at heading scale) sit behind the circular portraits to add depth without adding contrast.
